source: Traced from OCH architectural CAD files (DWG), 9/28/26. Supersedes the raster traces of 9/22/26.
method: dwg2dxf (LibreDWG, built from source — dwgread -O JSON is unreliable on these files), then ezdxf. Layer A-Area-Masonry carries CLOSED finish-face area polylines, one per area (living, garage, porches). Union the ones forming the first-floor footprint: the total equals the sheet's stated slab figure, and the living figure equals the plan library's A/C square footage — two independent confirmations. Model space holds several copies; pick the connected shape whose WIDTH matches the plan. Where a plan has per-elevation floor plans, each is labelled FIRST FLOOR/ELEC "A"|"B"|"C" in nearby MTEXT — match by proximity, never by guessing from the filename. The garage sits at 86-88% of depth in every plan, so the alley end is the high-y end; outlines here are flipped so the garage is at y=0. Units in the DWG are inches. See claude/plan-geometry-from-cad.md.
keying: Entries are keyed by plan id (holland_a) where the elevations differ, and by family (addison) where they share one first-floor plan. Look up the plan id first and fall back to the family.

validation: Every footprint matches the plan library's width and depth and the sheet's stated slab area to within a square foot. Unlike the 9/22 raster traces there is no wall-line undercount, so areaSf equals slabSf rather than running 49-59 sf under it.
openDoors:
RESOLVED 10/3/26. Every overhead door is 16'-0" (OCH spec, confirmed by Brandi) and sits centred on the garage. Garage positions come from the A-Area-Masonry polygons, so every door is now CAD-derived rather than read off a raster trace.

The rule was validated against the one plan where the door is measured directly: Pearl's DWG carries a full A-Wall layer, and the gap between wall runs on its alley face gives 11.63 -> 27.63 ft. Pearl's garage centre is 19.63, so centre +/- 8.00 gives 11.63 -> 27.63. Exact, to the hundredth.

The previous traced values ran 15.29-15.93 ft wide and sat 0.05-0.45 ft off centre; the largest correction was Parker at 0.45 ft. A-Wall-Open was investigated as a direct source and does NOT carry the overhead door on any of these files — its longest runs are 13-14.7 ft and belong to other openings.

Holland and Knox have three first-floor plans each, but the garage sits at an IDENTICAL x in all three (Holland 14.25-34.83, Knox 14.33-34.92), so one door position is correct for every elevation. That is measured, not inherited.
